title: Functions, errors and defer
summary: Multiple return values, variadic functions, errors as values, wrapping, defer and recover.
hints: `Divide` returns `(0, ErrDivideByZero)` when `b == 0`, otherwise `(a / b, nil)`. Returning a package-level sentinel error (not a fresh `errors.New` each time) is what lets callers test for it with `errors.Is`.
`MinMax(xs ...int)`: inside, `xs` is a plain `[]int`. Return `ErrEmpty` when `len(xs) == 0`; otherwise start with `lo, hi := xs[0], xs[0]` and loop. Callers pass a slice with `MinMax(nums...)`.

`ParsePositive`: call `strconv.Atoi(s)`; if it fails, `return 0, fmt.Errorf("parse %q: %w", s, err)`, where `%w` wraps the original error so `errors.As` can still find the `*strconv.NumError`. For `n <= 0` wrap the sentinel: `fmt.Errorf("parse %q: %w", s, ErrNotPositive)`. For `Try`, `defer` a function that calls `recover()` and assigns to the *named* result `err`. For `DeferOrder`, deferred calls run last-in first-out after the function body, and they can modify named results.
